plan: My private value is $20. Since this is a first-price sealed bid auction with a unique payment rule (third-highest bid), I want to bid strategically. I'll aim to bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk significant loss. A bid around $22-$25 seems reasonable - high enough to likely win, but not excessively risky given my $20 value.

My private value is $29. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This prevents overpaying if I win and ensures I win when the item is truly worth more to me than others. Since values are randomly drawn, I can't predict others' values. Bidding $29 maximizes my potential profit - I'll win if my value is higher than others, and pay less than my value if I win.

With a private value of $45, I want to maximize my potential profit. Since this is a first-price sealed bid auction where I pay the third-highest bid, I'll bid strategically near my true value. Given the value range is $0-$49, other bidders might bid around $20-$40. I'll bid $42 - slightly below my true value to leave room for potential profit, but high enough to likely win the auction.
